What it still cannot do. The stand-still command comes 0.3 to 0.5 s after someone steps out of the hedge (revision 6: up to 0.7 s); stopping from 1.0 m/s takes about a second more. Under about 1 m in front of the nose at the fast cruise the robot is still braking when they meet: at the full 1.0 m/s a walker 0.4 m ahead was touched at up to 0.22 m/s and a running child at up to 0.86 m/s; from 1.0 m the robot stopped 0.07 to 0.23 m short in three runs and the walker brushed the nose corner at under 0.01 m/s in a fourth. Not found: someone with their back within about 0.1 m of the hedge (revision 6: 0.3 to 0.5 m); someone already standing near a turn before the robot arrives, outside the nose circle and out of the camera's view; anything lower than 0.30 m (camera only, then the nose strip).

Every detection figure is assumed: lidar 10 scans a second, 10 mm noise; a person is a 0.5 m disc (a small child 0.3 m); camera 5 pictures a second, 60 % at night. [6.1] The cases were run again on a spoiled lidar (15 and 30 % of returns lost, 30 and 60 % more from a person, false returns, a ragged, swaying hedge): trips complete at both levels with no false stop in the lane; results in the revision 6.1 note, section 2. Measuring the real sensors is still the first job on the built robot.
